TECH3_2021-41.exp: Analogous estimating uses historical/similar-project data as a quick top-down proxy, which makes it generally less accurate than bottom-up or parametric methods that use more detailed data.

TECH3_2021-42.exp: The cost baseline is an output of Determine Budget, not an input to it, and the requirements traceability matrix is a scope-management artifact not used here; scope baseline, agreements, basis of estimates/cost estimates, risk register, and resource management plan are all genuine Determine Budget inputs per PMBOK's ITTO list.

TECH3_2021-43.exp: Cost Plus Fixed Fee is a cost-reimbursable contract that guarantees the contractor's costs are covered plus a fixed profit regardless of overruns, putting the least risk on the contractor -- unlike fixed-price contracts, which push cost risk onto the seller.

TECH3_2021-44.exp: PMBOK defines Determine Budget as aggregating the estimated costs of individual activities or work packages to establish an authorized cost baseline, matching option B exactly.

TECH3_2021-45.exp: Cost Management runs Plan Cost Management, Estimate Costs, Determine Budget, then Control Costs -- i.e. ii, iii, i, iv.

TECH3_2021-46.exp: Control chart upper and lower control limits are set using statistical calculations (typically plus/minus three standard deviations from the process mean), not a Pareto chart or ROM estimate.

TECH3_2021-47.exp: An outside team checking whether project work complies with organizational and PMI policies, standards, and procedures is the textbook definition of a Quality Audit.

TECH3_2021-48.exp: A component-specific tool used to verify that a defined set of required steps has been performed is a Checklist, a standard quality-management tool.

TECH3_2021-49.exp: A monitoring and evaluation framework is generally built around objectives, the assumptions underlying them, measurable indicators, and a summary of planned activities -- the most complete of the four options; the shorter options (just objectives/indicators, or goal/objectives) omit necessary elements.

TECH3_2021-50.exp: Stakeholder analysis, SWOT analysis, and problem tree analysis are all standard situational-analysis tools used before project/program planning.

TECH3_2021-51.exp: Proactive correspondence, luncheon meetings, and symposia are all named PMBOK examples of networking activities used to build professional relationships; 'organization management' is a broad management function, not a specific networking activity.

TECH3_2021-52.exp: With team members spread across Kolkata, Guwahati, Bangalore, and Aizawl, a deliberate communication plan (methods, frequency, channels for a geographically dispersed team) becomes essential to keep everyone aligned, more so than team-building or status reporting alone.

TECH3_2021-53.exp: PMBOK states that once ground rules are established, all project team members share responsibility for enforcing them, not just the project manager.

TECH3_2021-54.exp: 'Recruitment and retention of qualified employees' is a fixed, widely used HR collocation describing a core employer goal; the blank needs a single word pairing naturally with 'retention', which fits recruitment far better than training or development.

TECH3_2021-55.exp: Job evaluation establishes a systematic, objective basis for comparing job worth, which is the standard preventive tool used to reduce subjective disagreements among rating-committee members; this draws on general HR management terminology rather than PMBOK, so confidence is limited.

TECH3_2021-56.exp: The basic communication model runs: sender encodes the message, transmits it through a medium, the receiver decodes it, acknowledges receipt, and then provides feedback/response -- i.e. Encode, Transmit, Decode, Acknowledge, Feedback.

TECH3_2021-57.exp: PMBOK's ITTO explicitly makes Work Performance Reports an output of the Monitor and Control Project Work process, which belongs to Project Integration Management; work performance information (not reports) is what gets aggregated from the individual controlling processes.

TECH3_2021-58.exp: A detailed written report to the client documenting a major cost impact (100 lakh) from a schedule crash is a formal, official form of communication -- written, deliberate, and part of the project's documented record, not an informal or unofficial exchange.

TECH3_2021-59.exp: Communication with external parties (clients, vendors, regulators) tends to be formal and documented for accountability, so it is dominated by written documents, unlike internal communication which is often more verbal/informal.

TECH3_2021-60.exp: The project manager is the hub through which all project communication is planned, filtered, and directed, making the PM the critical element of the communication system rather than any single report or directive.
